name: Bulkamid pivotal trial
question: Is urethral Bulkamid injection noninferior to Contigen collagen injection for female stress urinary incontinence?

design.population: Women with stress urinary incontinence or stress-predominant mixed urinary incontinence at North American study centers.
design.locator: Sokol 2014, PubMed abstract, Materials and Methods and Results

verdictNote: Noninferiority was reported for the composite leakage and episode response at one year.
takeaway: In women with stress or stress-predominant mixed incontinence, Bulkamid polyacrylamide hydrogel injection was noninferior to Contigen collagen gel injection for at least 50% reduction in both leakage and incontinence episodes at one year (53.2% versus 55.4% in the journal report).

reports.label: One-year randomized comparison
reports.citation: Sokol ER, Karram MM, Dmochowski R. "Efficacy and Safety of Polyacrylamide Hydrogel for the Treatment of Female Stress Incontinence: A Randomized, Prospective, Multicenter North American Study." *J Urol.* 2014;192(3):843-849. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2014.03.109
reports.followUpLocator: PubMed abstract, Materials and Methods and Results

results.measure: At least 50% reduction in both leakage and incontinence episodes at 12 months
results.note: The abstract reports noninferiority but gives no margin, confidence interval, or analysis denominators.

results.measure: Patient-reported zero stress episodes at 12 months
Patient-reported cured or improved at 12 months

delivery.label: Injection schedule
delivery.value: Up to three urethral submucosal injections at one-month intervals
delivery.locator: PubMed abstract, Purpose and Materials and Methods

reports.label: One-year patient characteristics analysis
reports.citation: Elmelund M, Sokol ER, Karram MM, et al. "Patient Characteristics that May Influence the Effect of Urethral Injection Therapy for Female Stress Urinary Incontinence." *J Urol.* 2019;202(1):125-131. doi:10.1097/JU.0000000000000176

results.endpoint: Pooled post hoc cure and improvement
results.measure: One-year outcome among both agents combined
results.note: Among 291 analyzed women (191 Bulkamid, 100 Contigen), 74 (25%) were cured, 164 (56%) improved, and 53 (18%) had no effect. Age at least 60 years and fewer than 2.5 daily stress episodes were associated with cure; 90% had an effect and 38% were cured in that subgroup versus 13% cured among younger women with at least 2.5 episodes.
